terms.loan: Money you borrow now and promise to pay back later, a little at a time.
terms.interest: The extra money you pay for borrowing. The longer you owe, the more it adds up.
terms.apr: The interest you pay in one year, shown as a percent of what you owe. 4% means $4 for every $100 you borrow, per year.
terms.elasticity: How much visitors change their minds when the ticket price changes. Raise the price and fewer people come; lower it and more show up.
terms.seasonality: Some times of year are busier than others. Summer brings crowds, winter is quiet, so plan your money around it.
terms.cash_flow: Money coming in versus money going out. Even a great park can run out of cash if bills arrive before ticket money does.
terms.profit: What is left after you subtract every cost from every dollar you earned. Above zero is good, below zero means you lost money.
terms.tax: A share of your profit that goes to the government. You only pay it when you actually made money.
terms.capacity: The most visitors your park can handle in one day. Upgrading the parking lot raises the limit.
terms.net_worth: Everything you own, like land, fences, dinosaurs, and cash, minus everything you owe.
terms.upkeep: The small regular cost of keeping things working. Fences and upgraded facilities charge it every quarter whether visitors come or not.
terms.auction: A sale where buyers take turns offering more money. The highest offer wins, so it can be a bargain or a trap.
terms.debt: The total amount you still owe the bank.
terms.debt_cap: The most the bank will let you owe. It grows with what your park is worth. What counts is your debt minus the cash you hold: if that stays above the cap for three quarters in a row, the bank takes the park.
terms.overdraft: Spending money you do not have. Bills like payroll still get paid, but the bank charges extra interest on the negative balance.
terms.revenue: All the money coming in from tickets and snacks, before paying any bills.
terms.expenses: All the money going out: salaries, food, upkeep, and interest.
terms.salary: What you pay each staff member every month, whether the park was busy or not.
terms.attendance: How many visitors came through the gate in a day.
terms.park_rating: A score from 1 to 5 stars for how good your park is. Cleanliness, variety, and happy visitors raise it.
terms.cleanliness: How tidy the park is. Visitors notice dirt, and a messy park earns fewer stars and fewer return trips.
terms.reputation: What people say about your park. Good news raises it, breakouts and accidents lower it.
terms.morale: How happy your staff are. Low morale means people quit; a manager and steady pay keep it up.
terms.concessions: Snacks and souvenirs. Every visitor spends a little extra once the food stand or gift shop is open, and more as they upgrade.
terms.advertising: Paying to tell more people about your park. It boosts visitors for a while, then wears off.
terms.quarter: Three months, or 90 days. Interest, taxes, and your report all come due at the end of each one.
terms.foreclosure: When you owe too much for too long, the bank takes the park and the game ends.
terms.fence_tier: How strong a fence is. Big or aggressive dinosaurs need stronger fences or they break out; small herbivores stay put behind any fence that meets their minimum.
terms.what_if: A preview of what would probably happen if you made this choice. It is an estimate, not a promise.
terms.prize: A reward for investing in the park. Spend at the General Store, or hit a milestone, and the park earns a decoration that visitors like.
terms.management_capacity: How many staff the Park Office can run smoothly. Go over it and morale slips a little each month until you upgrade the office.
terms.appeal: How attractive the park is to visitors: dinosaur popularity, variety, cleanliness, plus the Visitor Center and prizes.
terms.biome: The kind of land in a pen: desert, plains or marsh. Every species has a home biome it prefers. In the wrong one it is unhappy: fewer visitors care about it and its health slips.
terms.vegetation: Plants growing inside a pen. Seeds are an investment: pay once, and the pen grows free food every day after. Buying plants is a recurring cost that never stops. Marsh grows fastest, desert slowest.
terms.auto_restock: A standing order with the General Store: when a food runs low it is bought and charged for you, so nobody starves while you are busy elsewhere.
terms.days_of_food: How many days the park can feed its animals from what is in stock, at today's appetite. Below five days is a warning; at zero they start to starve.
terms.membership: A season pass. Members pay once a quarter instead of per visit, keep coming even in slow seasons, and leave if the park gets worse. Steady money, but only while the park stays good.
terms.churn: The share of members who do not renew at the end of a quarter. A low park rating makes more of them leave.
terms.campaign: A marketing push: it costs money up front and brings extra visitors for a while. Bigger ones need something worth advertising first.
terms.relandscape: Change the land type of a pen. It costs a share of the land price and clears any vegetation, so choose the biome carefully when you buy.
terms.goal: A long-term target for the park. The Goals panel shows every rung of the ladder with how close you are, and each one fires once when you reach it.
terms.grand_park: The top of the ladder: every facility at its best tier, every spend prize earned, and five stars held for four quarters in a row. Earn it and a plaque goes up at the gate.
terms.report_card: At the end of year five the park is graded A to F on profit, attendance, dinosaur welfare, education and guest satisfaction. The game keeps going afterwards; the card stays in Reports.
terms.welfare: How well the animals are looked after: average health, and a penalty for every death and every escape.
terms.education: How much visitors learn: the Visitor Center tier, how often the Fact Book is opened, and whether the school program has run.
terms.reduce_motion: Turns off shakes, floating numbers, slides and the delivery truck. Everything still happens, it just appears in place.
terms.difficulty: The difficulty mode is chosen when a park is founded and fixed for the run. Relaxed: bigger cheap loan, more visitors, no foreclosure. Standard: the tuned game. Classic: a shoestring loan, dearer bills, one quarter of grace.
terms.overhead: A fixed charge every quarter for owning land. Part of the bill is a flat fee no matter how much you own, and part grows with every tile you hold. Land costs money even when it earns nothing, so buying parcels you are not ready to use drains cash.
terms.bank_warning: Your debt minus your cash is above the debt cap. On Relaxed the bank never forecloses, but the overdraft still costs interest every quarter and the warning stays until you are back under the cap.

first_quarter_tips.title: Land comes in three types
first_quarter_tips.text: When you buy a parcel you choose Desert, Plains or Marsh. The biome sets the price and which species feel at home (the Fact Book lists each one).

first_quarter_tips.title: Seeds save money
first_quarter_tips.text: Open a pen and plant seeds: the greenery grows every day and herbivores graze it before touching bought plants. Marsh grows fastest.

first_quarter_tips.title: Never run out of food
first_quarter_tips.text: General Store -> Food (or Settings): turn on auto-restock and the store buys more when stock runs low. The Park bar shows days of food left.

first_quarter_tips.title: Climb the marketing ladder
first_quarter_tips.text: Marketing shows every campaign in order. Cheap flyers first; bigger pushes unlock as the park grows. Memberships turn visitors into steady quarterly income.

first_quarter_tips.title: Check your goals
first_quarter_tips.text: Park bar -> Goals: repay the loan, reach a net worth target, ten species, a five-star quarter, then the Grand Park. Year five brings a report card.
